description.narrative:
Interpeace har ansökt om 77 miljoner SEK i stöd för att genomföra insatsen '’Reinforcing community capacity for social cohesion and reconciliation through Societal Trauma Healing in Rwanda’, 2021-2025, mellan juli 2021 till juni 2022. Insatsen genomförs i samarbete med Prison Fellowship Rwanda (RFP), Haguruka och Dignity in Detention Organisation (DiDe).
Insatsens mål syftar till att stärka den mentala hälsan hos de som drabbats av folkmordet mot Tutsierna 1994 och deras emotionella och finansiella resiliens och i längde verka för hållbar fred. Mer specifikt syftar insatsen på att stärka återintegreringen av fängelsfångar dömda för folkmordsbrott som kommer att släppas under de kommande fyra åren och minska risker relaterad till återintegreringen, såsom förväntade ökade fall av könsbaserat våld, spänningar, konflikter och ökade nivåer av trauma. Insatsen arbetar även mer Rwandas yngre befolkning för att minska intergenerationstrauma och därmed motverka radikalisering och ökade spänningar bland den yngre generationen. Programmet är uppdelat i fyra resultatområden med specifika mål och aktiviteter, (1) Förbättrad läkning och psykosocial motståndskraft bland män, kvinnor och unga i samhället och inom fängelser, (2) Förbättrad social sammanhållning och återintegrering av folkmordsdömda fängelsegångar (3) Inkluderande och kollektiva försörjningsmöjligheter för män, kvinnor och unga i samhället och fängelser för att förbättra välbefinnandet, social samanhållning och försoning, och (4) Stärkande av nationell policy och program inom ramen för helande, social sammanhållning och försoning, samt försörjningsmöjligheter för de fattigaste, inklusive släppta fängelsefångar och de som överlevde folkmordet mot Tutsierna.
Sverige står som enskild finansiär av insatsen men förhoppningen är antalet givare kommer att öka under insatsens gång vid en eventuell utökning av insatser till andra distrikt. CKCK MSK kommer vidareförmedlas till partnerorganisationer samt TVET-institutioner.

Interpeace has submitted to the Embassy a proposal for a four-year programme titled, ’Reinforcing community capacity for social cohesion and reconciliation through Societal Trauma Healing in Rwanda’. The proposed duration of the programme is July 2021 to June 2025, and the budget is 77 million SEK. The contribution will be implemented in close collaboration with Prison Fellowship Rwanda ( RFP), HAGURUKA and Dignity in Detention Organization (DiDe).
The proposed programme aims to address and heal the psycho-social wounds that has been caused by the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi and strengthen social cohesion, trust building and socio-economic development with the longer perspective of promoting sustainable peace in Rwanda. This will be achieved through trauma healing, community dialogue, and small-scale livelihood projects. A strong emphasis is put on the releases of prisoners convicted of crimes relating to the Genocide against the Tutsi and their reintegration back into their communities as well as on youth, and their ability to heal from inter-generational trauma. The program is divided into four result areas with specific goals and activities, (1) Improved healing and psychosocial resilience among men, women and young people in society and in prisons, (2) Improved social cohesion and reintegration of genocidal convictions (3) Inclusion and collective livelihoods for men, women and young people in society and prisons for the development of well-being, social cohesion and reconciliation; genocide survivor.
Sweden is the sole financier of the contribution, but there is an anticipation that additional donors will fund a potential up-scale of the programme. CKCK MSK will be passed on to partner organizations and TVET institutions.

The objective of the programme is to strengthen psychosocial and socioeconomic resilience for sustainable peace among communities in five districts in Rwanda through five outcomes:
Enhanced healing and psychosocial resilience among men, women, youth and other vulnerable groups in communities and prisons.
Enhanced social cohesion and prisoners psychosocial reintegration.
Improved socio-economic inclusion and collective livelihood opportunities for men, women, youth, and other vulnerable groups.
National policies and programmes on healing, social cohesion and collective livelihoods are informed by lessons learned from programme interventions.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
The Societal Healing Programme in Rwanda had various interventions that took place in communities, health centers and correctional facilities as well as through awareness and dissemination events that strengthened the capacities of mental health professionals, deepened the social emotional and trauma informed leadership skills of local decisionmakers, and improved livelihoods. The programme has continued to contribute towards Rwanda's efforts to foster reconciliation and sustainable peace by addressing the linked issues of mental health, social cohesion and economic resilience.
1) Through socio therapy, the program has created safe and inclusive healing spaces in communities and facilitated open dialogues among the members, as well as mutual healing and cohesion, between genocide survivors, genocide perpetrators, returnees and combatants. During the reporting period, 1,945 people graduated from socio therapy healing spaces established in communities and in four correctional facilities (the adult facilities at Nyamagabe, Musanze, and Ngoma, and the juvenile facility at Nyagatare). Sociotherapy fostered trust and forgiveness among 1,541 participants (697 men, 844 women), in one hundred community spaces. 791 of the participants were adult and 750 were youth. After the intervention, 77.1% of participants reported that they were comfortable leaving their children with families of survivors or perpetrators, up from 62.6% before the therapy, which showed a significant increase in the level of trust among community members. Overall, 3,291 people (1,411 male and 1,880 female) were reached through 209 healing spaces, alongside 4,467 other targeted rights holders/duty bearers (2,140 female and 2,327 male).
2) Under Resilience oriented therapy (ROT): It was reported that an overall improvement in resilience levels was noted, measured through a system known as The Walsh family resilience scale. The key dimensions highlighted to have significant improvement was in (1) Emotional support and expression The scale noted encouraging open and supportive communication among community members. (2) Communication styles the index captured developing positive patterns for sharing and understanding (3) Conflict resolution the program was seen to have equipped families with tools for resolving disagreements effectively and (4) Listening and understanding the program was seen to have fostered attentive and empathetic interactions among community members that were once in conflict. Overall 32 spaces in 32 health centers, with 293 participants (81 men, 212 women) received resilience oriented therapy participants improved their adaptability. After the therapy, 65.5% reported that their resilience had improved, compared to 53.2% beforehand.
3) Co livelihood. The programme has managed to bring together former genocide perpetrators, survivors, and other vulnerable groups, along with their families, which has enabled them improve their living conditions while fostering a shared approach to constructing a peaceful and inclusive future. This co-livelihood component of the program encourages the development of new identities based on individual skills and contributions to society, rather than perpetuating divisive identities from the past. As a result, participants initiated income generating activities, such as small businesses and agricultural ventures, building on the trust and reconciliation acquired during their healing journeys. Participants also embraced professional approaches to managing enterprises, improved their savings and credit management (using tools such as savings books), and cultivated stronger ties with local authorities. Support was provided to 17 business initiatives, benefiting 234 individuals (116 men, 118 women). Participants gained economic independence and food security through training in financial literacy and business management. 40.7% achieved regular access to food and 56.4% improved their access to food.
4) Prisoner rehabilitation and reintegration: This protocol significantly helped participants to overcome psychological wounds and improve mental wellbeing. The manual designed through this program has helped former perpetrators and victims to manage anger and negative behaviors, and bring peace to their lives. The programme has allowed individuals to reconnect with their 'lost' others, helped individuals find emotional healing through sharing their pain, and enabled them rebuild trust with neighbors after years of resentment. Given the context it is noted that this is quite a sensitive yet fundamental activity in the program
